correctness.rationale: The spherical cosine laws establish the exact arc aperture and all positive parameter domains; spherical Gauss--Bonnet gives A and L with the proper curvature/corner signs; h(t)=asin(sin(t)/c) has the third derivative of h=s^2 cos(t)(c^2+2sin^2(t))/(c^2-sin^2(t))^(5/2), with strictly positive z-log derivative on the entire range. The integral Taylor remainder makes n^2(A_disk-A_n) strictly decreasing and convergent to pi^3 s^2/(12c), proving the sharp constants and endpoint equality. The packaged verify.py passed symbolic, high-precision, independent spherical cosine law and independent uniform-sphere area sampling checks. Numerical checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The regular spherical Reuleaux family is a canonical finite-corner interpolation between the sharp fixed-width area minimizer (Reuleaux triangle) and the area-maximizing disk. Exact finite-corner convergence is a natural geometric approximation question. The strictly monotone n^2 normalized deficit and two best possible coefficients furnish an all-width comparison of finite-corner approximations, not merely a trivial rearrangement of the general spherical Barbier identity or a formula restricted to w=pi/2. The precision of both constants and strictness supplies natural numerical benchmarks for spherical convex approximation.
